acceptance_criteria.criterion: renderStatusCard produces valid HTML with PID, elapsed time, progress summary, and status badge.
renderKillButton calls API.orchestratorKill() after a confirmation prompt and invokes the callback.
renderDismissButton calls API.orchestratorDismiss() and invokes the callback.
renderLogPreview auto-polls API.getRunLogEntries() and appends new events. Returns a cleanup function that stops polling.
renderProgressBadge maps lastAction to appropriate icon/color.
renderCliReference returns static HTML with the CLI commands reference.
All functions are accessible on the global OrchestratorWidgets object.
renderStatusCard(entry) returns an HTML string with a status badge (badge-pending / badge-started / badge-dead), PID, elapsed running time, and progress summary text.
renderKillButton(entryId, onDone) returns an HTMLButtonElement that calls window.confirm before calling API.orchestratorKill(entryId) and invokes onDone on success.
renderDismissButton(entryId, onDone) returns an HTMLButtonElement that calls API.orchestratorDismiss(entryId) and invokes onDone on success.

renderLogPreview(container, slug, filename) auto-polls API.getRunLogEntries() and appends new events to container as <div class="log-preview-entry"> elements. Returns a cleanup function that stops polling.

renderProgressBadge(lastAction) maps lastAction strings to badge classes: run_start/stage_start/progress_snapshot → badge-info, stage_complete/wp_complete → badge-success, run_end/heartbeat → badge-neutral, run_error/stage_error → badge-error, signal_shutdown → badge-warning, unknown/null → badge-neutral with idle label.
renderCliReference() returns a static HTML string containing the orchestrate, --resume, --dry-run, and kill-orchestrator command references, wrapped in a container div.
All functions are accessible on the global OrchestratorWidgets object. The module does not pollute the global namespace beyond this one name.

summary: Reviewed gui/public/js/orchestrator-widgets.js (new ES5 IIFE module, ~290 lines) and tests/gui/orchestrator-widgets.test.ts (41 tests covering all 7 ACs + 7 refined variants).
IIFE pattern correctly scopes all internals; only OrchestratorWidgets is placed on the global object (AC-7).
XSS protection verified: all user-controlled values go through escapeHtml(). renderLogPreview uses textContent not innerHTML. renderProgressBadge escapes lastAction.
renderLogPreview stopped-flag + clearInterval cleanup is correct and handles the async race (stale .then() callback blocked by stopped flag).
renderCliReference is static HTML with pre-escaped entities — no user data, no risk.
vm.runInThisContext() + jsdom is a valid approach for testing browser-side ES5 scripts in Vitest.
Fake timer usage (vi.useFakeTimers/useRealTimers) is isolated to the renderLogPreview describe block and correctly torn down.
Minor: two different promise-settling idioms coexist in tests (Promise.resolve x2 vs setTimeout(r,0)) — functional but inconsistent.

comments.note: XSS protection is thorough: all user-controlled values (pid, progress, elapsed, effectiveStatus label) pass through escapeHtml(). renderLogPreview uses textContent for DOM mutations. renderProgressBadge escapes lastAction. The redundant escapeHtml(meta.cls) and escapeHtml(mapping.color) on hardcoded strings is belt-and-suspenders — harmless.
renderLogPreview stopped-flag guard correctly handles the race: `if (stopped) return` inside the .then() callback prevents stale entries from being appended after cleanup(). Pattern is sound.

[documentation-forward] renderCliReference() embeds static CLI command text (orchestrate, --resume, --dry-run, kill-orchestrator.js). This content may drift from the actual CLI over time. Add an inline comment referencing where these commands are defined (scripts/ and orchestrator/) so future maintainers know to keep them in sync.

Tests use two different promise-settling idioms: `await Promise.resolve(); await Promise.resolve();` vs `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))`. Both work but `setTimeout(r, 0)` is more reliable for multi-hop .then() chains. Minor consistency improvement for future test additions.
No observations beyond the above — code is clean, ES5-correct, and well-structured.
